reason: The hypothesis relies on specific claims about V/Cr improving ductility, creating defect sinks, and preserving high-temperature BCC stability, but the cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address these claims. E1 explicitly warns that Cr promotes intermetallics that deteriorate plasticity, and E2 discusses irradiation resistance in an FCC Al0.1CoCrFeNi HEA, not BCC NbMoTaW or V/Cr effects. Thus, the key premises lack specific prior support and one is contradicted.
premises: V or Cr addition improves room-temperature ductility of BCC refractory HEAs
Dopant-induced nanoscale fluctuations or segregation act as defect sinks, improving irradiation tolerance
BCC matrix and high-temperature strength are preserved up to ~1600 °C with small dopant additions
Cr or V can be added without forming deleterious secondary phases that compromise plasticity
